Updating rzig in a package

Source: vignettes/updating.Rmd
updating.Rmd

A package created with use_rzig() contains a copy of the rzig framework (src/rzig/framework) and build files made from rzig’s templates (configure, src/Makevars.in, src/entry.c, src/rzig/build.zig and others). The framework and the R side of rzig must come from the same version, because the generated bindings rely on both. After an update of rzig, update_rzig() brings the package to the installed version. Every step of this vignette is plain R and needs no Zig compiler.

A package to update 

path <- file.path(tempdir(), "updatedpkg")
create_rzig_package(path, tests = FALSE)
#> Created package updatedpkg at /tmp/RtmpHzdwMC/updatedpkg
#> Write Zig functions in src/rzig/src/main.zig, then run rzig::document(path) and rzig::build_zig(path)

What the update does

update_rzig() replaces the framework sources, replaces each build file that is identical to a template of some rzig version (the package author has not changed it), adds missing files and regenerates the bindings. The package author’s Zig sources in src/rzig/src, the list of C libraries src/rzig/c_libraries.zon and every file rzig does not know stay as they are. On a package that is current, the result lists no file:

result <- update_rzig(path)
#> Generated RZig bindings for updatedpkg: 1 exported function
#> Updated RZig in package updatedpkg to rzig 1.0.0
result
#> RZig update of package updatedpkg
#>   everything matches the installed rzig

Customized build files are kept

A build file that the package author changed is kept, because the change may matter, and listed, so that it can be compared with the new template. Here src/Makevars.in gets an extra comment:

makevars <- file.path(path, "src", "Makevars.in")
cat("# Built with a custom flag.\n", file = makevars, append = TRUE)
result <- update_rzig(path)
#> Generated RZig bindings for updatedpkg: 1 exported function
#> Updated RZig in package updatedpkg to rzig 1.0.0
result
#> RZig update of package updatedpkg
#>   customized build files kept (compare with the templates of rzig) (1):
#>     src/Makevars.in

rzig_status() notes the difference without failing, because a customized build file is allowed:

status <- rzig_status(path)
status[status$step == "Scaffold", ]
#> RZig status of package updatedpkg
#>   [ok] Scaffold      build files and framework sources present
#>                      differs from the rzig template: src/Makevars.in

With force = TRUE, update_rzig() replaces customized build files with the templates as well:

result <- update_rzig(path, force = TRUE)
#> Generated RZig bindings for updatedpkg: 1 exported function
#> Updated RZig in package updatedpkg to rzig 1.0.0
result
#> RZig update of package updatedpkg
#>   customized build files replaced (1):
#>     src/Makevars.in

A framework from another version

When the framework files differ from those of the installed rzig, for example after install.packages("rzig") in a project that was not updated, rzig_status() fails the scaffold step and names update_rzig(). A changed framework file shows the check:

framework_file <- file.path(path, "src", "rzig", "framework", "rzig.zig")
cat("// local change\n", file = framework_file, append = TRUE)
status <- rzig_status(path)
status[status$step == "Scaffold", ]
#> RZig status of package updatedpkg
#>   [--] Scaffold      1 framework file differs from rzig 1.0.0
#>                        (framework/rzig.zig); run update_rzig(path), which keeps
#>                        src/rzig/src and customized build files
#> 1 of 1 checks failed: Scaffold
result <- update_rzig(path)
#> Generated RZig bindings for updatedpkg: 1 exported function
#> Updated RZig in package updatedpkg to rzig 1.0.0
result
#> RZig update of package updatedpkg
#>   framework sources refreshed (1):
#>     src/rzig/framework/rzig.zig

Recommended routine

After updating rzig: run update_rzig(path), read the list of kept files, run rzig_status(path), rebuild with build_zig(path) and run the tests of the package. The NEWS file of rzig lists the changes of each version that affect packages.
